design_rationale:
WHY A GOOD TEST. Renee moved from Houston to Richmond: her Texas owner term was cancelled at her request on 2026-10-05 and a Virginia owner term started that day. She asks only to have her Florida SR-22 moved onto the Virginia policy. The moved certificate rule waits on two record states of the certificate it replaces: "The moved certificate fee for a certificate on an Owner Auto Policy term is not fixed until that certificate carries an SR-26 date and a certificate end date." and "The moved certificate fee is fixed only after the replaced certificate, when it rests on an Owner Auto Policy term, was requested for a reason that is charged a filing fee and had no fee reversed because it was withdrawn before transmission or was a duplicate request, shows a filing fee charge standing for its own request." The certificate rests on the Texas owner term and came by carrier_transfer, a charged reason, with no withdrawn or duplicate reversal, so both waits apply. The records show neither: no SR-26 although the Texas term ended, and all four fee charges (35.00 at the FR-44 rate on 2026-07-10, 25.00 coded as a new requirement on 2026-07-15, 50.00 billed for two certificates on 2026-08-14 and 25.00 re-sent as a duplicate by the September run on 2026-09-14) were reversed in full as company_error. The desk must transmit the cancellation SR-26 (four schedule rules), charge the fee again (six rules; it itself waits on the SR-26), then price the moved certificate on the new term (six rules) and hand the order to her. Every figure rests only on the publishable keys (XF 24-27), each dimension once: how coverage ended (the backing term's cancellation reason), how it was restored (lapse length), the certificate's standing with the state (its SR-26 and end dates), the company's state schedule by the backing term's state group, the filing state against that state, the certificate form the backing term is written to back, and the certificate type (which fixes the backing kind). No requirement-days, prior-filing, ledger, limits or plan key enters a factor; the fees start from flat company fees, so form is charged only once.

SCOPE. Task 0 occupies the lapse SR-26 (terms reinstated with a lapse) and the reinstatement refiling. Task 1 claims fr_ext_cancellation_sr26_runoff (transmit_cancellation_sr26_eaec830f: the SR-26 for any backing term cancelled and not reinstated), fr_ext_unbilled_fee (post_unbilled_filing_fee_f14427ed) and fr_ext_moved_refiling_fee (order_moved_certificate_231455f7). Each sibling overwrite of the fee clause names the other two cases; the certificate-end clause overwrites name each other; the one-open clause is overwritten for the state_change replacement only.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Draw: prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[4,6,6] -> cancellation SR-26 4, fee charged again 6, moved certificate 6. Root fr_ext_moved_refiling_fee (owner=user). Edges: moved -> cancellation SR-26 (value_input on transfer_basis, state form, negated); moved -> fee charged again (state_gate on fr_filings.fees_charged_total, state form, affirmative; "standing" excludes the reversed July charge, so the stale record cannot satisfy it); fee -> cancellation SR-26 (value_input on recharge_basis, state form, negated; scoped to "the filing it is charged on, when that filing's Owner Auto Policy backing term has been cancelled"). False at the opening: fr_filings.<SR-22>.status = filed, sr26_date = "", certificate_end_date = "" with auto_policies.<Texas>.status = cancelled, closed_date 2026-10-05; fr_filing_transactions show 135.00 charged and 135.00 waived (four company_error reversals), fees_charged_total 0.00. Exactly one write sets an SR-26 date on a certificate whose backing term was cancelled and not reinstated (the cancellation SR-26) and exactly one charges a fee on an existing filing (the fee charged again). Skip runs: no SR-26 -> fee charged again 44.00, moved fee 43.00; no fee charged again -> the moved certificate is ordered with its gate unmet and the 32.00 fee row is missing (gold 32.00 / 31.00). Order pinned: SR-26, fee, moved certificate. No deadlock: the SR-26 waits on nothing and a late one is still sent at once (run-off from its actual transmission), and the fee charged again never falls below its 10.00 minimum while its cap (fees reversed less fee standing) is above zero in its scope, so the standing-fee wait can always be met; the wait is carved out by record test for a non-owner backing, a reason that carries no fee, or a withdrawn or duplicate reversal. The persona names none of these problems.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Cancellation SR-26: term_coverage_ended holds (Texas term cancelled, not continued); not_before_end inherited (closed_date 2026-10-05 day 0, SR-26 2026-10-07; 2026-10-04 too early); timely is restated by the cancellation rule (day 0 the closed_date; on or before day 3 is timely, a later one is still sent at once with its run-off from its actual transmission; the lapse SR-26 keeps day 0 at the lapse_start_date; here day 2); release_conditions not engaged (copy only, no release request, required_through_date 2027-03-31 not reached). Fee charged again: the dedup sentence is restated (a fee reversed in full as charged in error is charged again once, so one fee stands). Moved certificate: one open filing per driver and state holds through the state_change exception once the old certificate is cancellation_filed; Florida is an SR-22 eligible state; the Virginia term is in force and its 100/300/50 package meets the Florida minimum (out-of-state filing, filing state's limits govern); the filer is the named insured (Owner-Operator) and the Corolla is scheduled on the Virginia term; one fee on the new filing.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Target: the SR-22 Owner-Operator certificate 1474f5d5 on CPA-TX-2417360. The cancellation SR-26 reads the Texas term's cancellation_reason (insured_request), closed_date (2026-10-05), package window, garaging_state (TX) and record, and the certificate's type and filing state (FL). The fee charged again reads the certificate's new SR-26 dates, its type and filing state, the Texas term's cancellation_reason, garaging_state, record and filing stamp (sr22), and the fee ledger only for its cap (135.00 reversed less 0.00 standing). The moved certificate reads the certificate's SR-26 dates, type and filing state, the Texas term's cancellation_reason, and the new term: the owner term with the latest new_business premium (CPA-VA-2560184, garaged VA, written to back an SR-22). Excluded: the converted Texas non-owner term (not a backing term), renewal premiums, plans and limits.

FACTOR CARD (publishable keys only, each dimension once; state groups FL/VA, TX/GA, AZ/OH). Cancellation run-off (4), baseline 10: cancel_runoff_counting (method) insured_request from the closed_date 10 - 2 = 8 (result with it at baseline 17); cancel_state_notice TX +2 (13); cancel_out_of_state_notice FL vs TX different groups +3 (12, multi-source); cancel_type_notice Owner-Operator +2 (13). All-baseline 10 != 15. Fee charged again (6), baseline recharge_base_fee 25.00: recharge_fee_method (method) still certified -> 13.00 (44.00); recharge_ending_charge insured_request +2.00 (30.00); recharge_state_charge TX +3.00 (29.00); recharge_out_of_state_charge +8.00 (24.00, multi-source); recharge_type_charge Owner-Operator +4.00 (28.00); recharge_form_charge SR-22 +2.00 (30.00); minimum 10.00 and cap 135.00 not engaged. All-baseline 25.00 != 32.00. Moved certificate (6), baseline transfer_base_fee 25.00: transfer_fee_method (method) still certified -> 13.00 (43.00); transfer_ending_charge insured_request +2.00 (29.00); transfer_state_charge new term VA +6.00 (25.00); transfer_out_of_state_charge FL vs VA same group +4.00 (27.00, multi-source); transfer_type_charge Owner-Operator +4.00 (27.00); transfer_form_charge SR-22 +2.00 (29.00). All-baseline 25.00 != 31.00. Every ladder has three tiers reachable inside its policy's scope; no method reads the fee ledger. Near-miss: the Texas new_business premium of 2026-07-10 is older than the Virginia one. No factor reads another factor's binding.

WORLD ROWS. Customer (Richmond, profile 2026-01-12); converted Texas non-owner term (548.00, conversion return 548.00 x 5/181 = 15.14) with its plan (paid 568.00, refund 15.14); Texas owner term (1164.00, insured-request return 1164.00 x 87/184 - 15.00 = 535.37 for 87 days (97 days less the SR-22's 10 run-off days; moved out of state, so nothing retained; Four-Pay plan charge 15.00)) with its signed cancellation request, Corolla, and Four-Pay plan (down 351.00 = 291.00 + 25.00 + 35.00; 35.00 waived company_error and netted on invoice 1 = 266.00; invoice 2 301.00 paid; invoice 3 issued; return credited; credit balance -234.37 to be refunded within credit_refund_days); Virginia owner term (1296.00, policy fee 25.00) with the Corolla and its Monthly EFT plan (signed bank authorization 2026-10-03, down 245.32 = 17% of 1296.00 + 25.00, balance 1075.68 for five installments from 2026-11-05); the certificate, its eight fee rows (four charges with distinct errors: 35.00 on 2026-07-10 at the FR-44 rate because Florida is an FR-44 state, 25.00 on 2026-07-15 at the right rate but coded new_requirement, 50.00 on 2026-08-14 billed for a Florida and a Texas certificate though only the Florida one exists, 25.00 on 2026-09-14 re-sent for the same request by the September billing run; and their four full company_error reversals on 2026-07-12, 2026-07-16, 2026-08-17 and 2026-09-16; only the first charge reached the Four-Pay plan, billed with the down payment and its reversal netted on invoice 1; the three later charges were reversed before the next invoice, so the plan never billed them) and its copy.

STANDARD SOLUTION. find_customers (8045552318) -> verify -> fr filings/transactions/documents -> auto policies/premium/changes/cancellation requests -> nonowner rows -> billing plans/transactions/invoices/authorizations -> transmit_cancellation_sr26_eaec830f (fr_filing_id, Texas auto_policy_id, runoff_days 15; end 2026-10-22) -> post_unbilled_filing_fee_f14427ed (fee_amount 32.00) -> her order_moved_certificate_231455f7 (customer_id, fr_filing_id, Virginia auto_policy_id, nonowner_policy_id null, filing_fee 31.00). check_compute --task 1 recomputes 15, 32.00 and 31.00 at handling time and every sensitivity figure; probes (decoy non-owner term, nonpayment and underwriting cancellations, non-owner backed certificate, late SR-26, end date passed, filing with no SR-26, cap and minimum edges, decoy reversal, later renewal and new-business premiums, new term in the filing state, moved after a nonpayment cancellation) are in worklog.md.
user_scenario:
You are Renee Hollister, thirty-six, a hospital billing specialist who has just moved from Houston to Richmond, Virginia, for a new job. Florida requires you to keep an SR-22 on file after your license was suspended there for driving uninsured on a visit to Orlando last spring, and Cardinal Point has been filing it on your Texas car policy. When you moved you had the Texas policy cancelled as of October 5 and took out a new Cardinal Point policy on the same Corolla here in Virginia starting that day. You are calling, practical and a little rushed between meetings, to get your Florida SR-22 moved onto the new Virginia policy so Florida never sees a gap. You want to place that order yourself, and you know it comes with a filing fee.
When the agent asks to verify you, you give your phone number, 8045552318, and your date of birth, 1990-04-12; if a third detail is wanted, your ZIP code is 23220. Your email, rhollister.va@gmail.com, you give only if asked for it. If asked for policy numbers, the old Texas one is CPA-TX-2417360 and the new Virginia one is CPA-VA-2560184. If asked how your name and license read on the Florida filing, it is Renee Marie Hollister, license number 24182293, and the Florida case number is 2603791; you say these only when asked.
If the agent tells you something has to be taken care of on the company's side first, you tell them to go ahead with whatever is needed. When the agent tells you the fee and hands you the order to submit, with the references it needs, you submit it yourself with exactly the references and the amount the agent gave you. You do not know what the fee should be and you do not argue about it. Once the order goes through and you have the new filing reference, you thank the agent and end the call.

edges.condition: For a replaced certificate on an Owner Auto Policy term cancelled and not reinstated, its fr_filings row carries a non-empty sr26_date and certificate_end_date (status cancellation_filed) at the handling time of the moved certificate.
edges.policy_source: The moved certificate fee for a certificate on an Owner Auto Policy term is not fixed until that certificate carries an SR-26 date and a certificate end date.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The Texas term was cancelled on 2026-10-05 but the certificate is still filed with no SR-26 date and no certificate end date.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The cancellation SR-26 sets cancellation_filed, sr26_date 2026-10-07 and certificate_end_date 2026-10-22; the transfer fee basis moves from 25.00 to 13.00 and the moved certificate fee from 43.00 to 31.00.

edges.condition: For such a replaced certificate, the fees charged on it less the fees reversed on it are above zero at the handling time of the moved certificate.
edges.policy_source: The moved certificate fee is fixed only after the replaced certificate, when it rests on an Owner Auto Policy term, was requested for a reason that is charged a filing fee and had no fee reversed because it was withdrawn before transmission or was a duplicate request, shows a filing fee charge standing for its own request.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The replaced certificate rests on an owner term, was requested for carrier_transfer (a charged reason), had no fee reversed as withdrawn or duplicate, and all four of its fee charges were reversed in full for company_error, so no fee stands.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The fee charged again books 32.00 on 2026-10-07, raising the replaced certificate's fees_charged_total from 0.00 to 32.00, so the gate the moved certificate waits on holds.

edges.condition: When the filing's own Owner Auto Policy backing term is cancelled, that filing's fr_filings row carries a non-empty sr26_date and certificate_end_date (status cancellation_filed) at the handling time of the fee charged again; for a term cancelled and not reinstated the cancellation SR-26 brings it about.
edges.policy_source: A fee charged again is not fixed until the filing it is charged on, when that filing's Owner Auto Policy backing term has been cancelled, carries an SR-26 date and a certificate end date.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Pinned by prerequisite sentences: the fee charged again 'is not fixed until the filing it is charged on, when that filing's Owner Auto Policy backing term has been cancelled, carries an SR-26 date and a certificate end date'; the moved certificate waits on the SR-26 dates and on a fee standing. The reverse order (fee before SR-26) charges 44.00 instead of 32.00, a different terminal state, so only the pinned order is gold. No deadlock: a late SR-26 is still sent at once with its run-off from its actual transmission, and the fee charged again never falls below its 10.00 minimum while its cap (fees reversed less fee standing) is above zero in its scope, so its write always leaves a fee standing.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the SR-26: the replaced certificate keeps no SR-26 date or end date (precondition unmet); computed mechanically the fee charged again is 44.00 and the moved certificate fee 43.00 instead of 32.00 / 31.00; the old certificate stays filed.

State gate: skipping the fee charged again leaves no fee standing on the replaced certificate (fees_charged_total 0.00); the terminal state lacks the 32.00 fee row and the moved certificate is ordered while its gate is unmet.
Skipping the SR-26 before the fee charged again: the re-charge fee basis stays 25.00 and fee_amount is 44.00 instead of 32.00.
